brief.headline: Close the 16.6% price gap on our biggest bottle SKU and move payment to 15 days in exchange for faster cash — worth about 10% to them.

priceAsk.summary: Ask them to match Suraj Blow Plast's price on the amber PET bottle (our biggest item with them) and review the cap pricing against the market benchmark.
priceAsk.target: ₹1.87/NOS for the PET BOT AMBER 100ML/25MM NECK 12.5G; market caps run ₹0.65–0.80/pc at volume
priceAsk.basis: We pay ₹2.18/NOS but Suraj gives us ₹1.87/NOS — a 16.6% gap. Closing it saves us ₹28644 a year. The market line for 28 mm PP caps shows ₹0.55–1.20/pc asking prices, typically ₹0.85–0.95/pc, with headroom down to ₹0.65–0.80/pc at higher volume — so there's room to negotiate if our cap pricing is above that band.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 30 days to 15 days after receipt in exchange for a small price cut.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Paying 15 days earlier frees up ₹46539 of our cash, but they borrow money at about 10.27% — so every rupee they get 15 days sooner is worth roughly 0.4% to them. Offer that saving as a trade for the faster payment.

brief.financialLeverage: TPAC is in reasonable shape — an [ICRA] A / Stable rating, they keep about ₹4 of every ₹100 they sell, and they have ₹35.20 Cr of free cash. But their cash is stuck for 79 days (same as similar firms at 79d), and they have GST and EPF filing delays — a grey-zone distress score of 2.77 means some strain. Still, we're tiny — just 0.02% of their ₹637.48 Cr revenue — so bundling more volume or showing them a strong second source (Manjushree, Mold-Tek) will give us the pull we need to close the price gap and tighten terms.

evidence.point: We pay 16.6% more than our best price on the main bottle SKU
evidence.figure: ₹2.18/NOS vs ₹1.87/NOS (Suraj Blow Plast); gap 16.6%; ₹28644 annual excess

evidence.point: They borrow at about 10.27%, so early payment is worth that rate to them

evidence.figure: GST filing delays; EPF payment delays

evidence.point: Their financial health is middling with some distress signs
evidence.figure: health score B (62/100); Altman Z 2.77 (grey zone)

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter at ₹2569.83 Cr revenue; health B (65/100); pharma bottles, caps, preforms — the top second-source candidate to put pressure on TPAC and secure supply.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader at ₹1010.97 Cr revenue; health B (73/100); pails, containers, pharma packaging — a strong, profitable alternate for bottles and closures.

alternates.name: Pearl Polymers Ltd
alternates.why: Listed PET bottle/jar specialist (Pearlpet brand) at ₹19.83 Cr revenue; direct fit for our PET bottles, though smaller and lower health at D (24/100) — worth a quote for the bottle SKU.

risks: We're only 0.02% of their business, so on our own we have little pull — bundle more SKUs, commit longer, or qualify Manjushree/Mold-Tek to create real competition.

Their compliance delays (GST, EPF) and grey-zone distress score (2.77) mean some operational strain — push for the price cut and faster payment, but watch delivery reliability and have a backup ready.
If we move to 15-day payment without a price cut in return, we give up ₹46539 of our cash and get nothing — make the payment shift conditional on closing the 16.6% gap.

The market line for caps (₹0.55–1.20/pc asking, ₹0.65–0.80/pc at volume) is a reference, not a quote we hold — use it to justify the target, but verify our actual cap pricing and volume before you lock a number.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to close the gap on the amber PET bottle — Suraj gives us ₹1.87 and you're at ₹2.18 — and in return we can look at moving payment from 30 days to 15, which puts cash in your hands faster.
